problems: The blind guess (standing humanoid or astronaut in a helmet) does not match the intended kettle. The lid dome and bail loop at the top read as a rounded helmet-like head, which pulls the viewer toward a figure.

The silhouette is upright and the key stars are mostly on the right parts: spout tip (25985) far left, spout-to-body junction (25606), foot (23685) at the bottom right, lid knob (24244) and flame tongues below.
The blue outline is a real silhouette, but the spout is a thin, weak wedge, and the body reads more as a rounded blob than a kettle.
The gold lines are drawn as a separate skeleton, and the flames are only thin triangles, so the figure lacks a clear kettle identity.
Labels overlap badly: the lid-crown and bail-top labels collide, and the 'rim of the body' and 'outer curve of the bail' labels run into each other, so the drawing is hard to read.
The star at the right wall of the body (23362) sits outside the body outline, not on the wall where the bail meets it.
output.advice: Redraw so the kettle reads clearly as a kettle. Widen the spout so it tapers from body wall to tip, with 25985 at the far tip and 25606 where the spout meets the left wall. Make the bail a clear arc from 24845 (left lug on the lid) over 23231 and 22479 down to 23362 on the right wall. Keep 24327 as the dome crown with 24244 as a knob directly above it, and 24305 just under the lid rim. Pull 23685 to the bottom-right foot and 24927 inside the base curve. Place the three flame tongues (25045, 24505, 23430) evenly below the base as a flame row, with 24505 tallest. Move labels into open space with leader lines so none overlap, and drop the gold skeleton or keep it thin so the blue silhouette carries the shape.
